items.prompt: A 4-bit up counter after 4'b1111 usually goes to…
items.explain: Fixed-width binary counters wrap on overflow.

items.prompt: The preferred hold pattern for a counter is…
choices: Use one always block with if (ce) count <= count + 1;
Drive count from two always blocks
Use blocking assignment in combinational logic only
Tie count to Z when idle
items.explain: Count enable keeps one sequential driver and clean hold behavior.

items.prompt: A modulo-10 counter wraps when q reaches…
choices: 15, because all 4-bit counters do the same thing
items.explain: Modulo counters add explicit wrap logic at the desired terminal count.

items.prompt: Gray counting is useful because adjacent output codes change only one bit at a time.
items.explain: That one-bit-change property is the key teaching point of Gray code sequences.
